**Finding submitted: deviation (INDEMN)**

- **Vendor side is largely satisfactory.** Section 10(a) requires Kubient to defend and indemnify AP and its personnel for third-party Claims arising from the Services, the Auction Platform, its breach of representations/warranties (which include the IP ownership warranties in 9(b)(vii)–(viii)), and its own and its subcontractors' acts or omissions. Section 11 provides standard notice, control-of-defence, consent-to-settlement and cooperation mechanics, and Section 7(a) carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion.
- **Deviation 1 — our indemnity is too broad.** Section 10(b) makes AP indemnify Kubient for breach of *any* representation or warranty plus an open-ended catch-all for "the acts or omissions of Customer or a third party ... under Customer's control," which is effectively an uncapped general indemnity rather than the narrow content-based indemnity the playbook allows.
- **Deviation 2 — knowledge qualifier on Creative.** Section 10(a)(iii) limits Kubient's indemnity for Creative served through its own Auction Platform to "the best of its knowledge," pushing third-party IP/content risk from Kubient's demand sources back onto AP.

Redline (validated ok:true): narrows 10(b) to the Content/Properties and AP's breach of applicable Law, and deletes the knowledge qualifier in 10(a)(iii).
